ms.promise: ADA Handle is building a Docker container that will allow any interested party access to all data associated with Handles and subHandles. This Docker container will allow any project, individual, dApp, wallet, etc. to run an instance -- that will contain Cardano Node, Ogmios, Kupo fully synced to Handles and subHandles -- and perform lookups for data associated with Handles and subHandles. For example, a user will be able to perform forward and reverse lookups, detecting the payment address associated with a subHandle or the other way around, by looking up a payment address and detecting a subHandle associated with it.
ms.criteria: The acceptance criteria for this milestone will be the delivery of Docker containers for PreProd, Preview and MainNet, that will allow any interested party to independently spin up an instance and run queries against the data.
ms.report:
We have completed the milestone. The ADA Handle API Docker Container and public API endpoint are ready. They can be verified here: https://github.com/koralabs/handles-public-api and here: https://koralabs.github.io/handles-public-api/.

The Docker Container can take up to 24 hours to sync, as it's running Cardano Node, and therefore needs to sync with the entire blockchain.

ms.promise: The current minting engine available at adahandle.com/mint mints unique rootHandles. This engine will be upgraded to mint NFT-based subHandles, issue and revoke Virtual subHandles.
ms.criteria: The acceptance criteria for this milestone will be the capability to mint NFT-based subHandles, issue and revoke Virtual subHandles, using a test policyID on the PreProd blockchain. ADA Handle will be able to, from our internal command-line interface, perform all actions related to subHandles. This milestone precedes the frontend implementation and therefore there won't be a GUI for the community to test from.

ms.promise:
The final outputs of this project will contain a fully operational subHandle minting portal, accessible from https://handle.me, that will detect rootHandles in users' wallets, allowing them to mint NFT-based subHandles, issue and revoke Virtual subHandles. This project will also deliver a decentralized API Docker container that the community can independently download and spin up to perform API queries for rootHandles and subHandles.
By the end of the project, all rootHandle owners will have the option to mint NFT-based subHandles, issue or revoke Virtual subHandles. The owner of the $acme rootHandle, for example, will connect to our minting portal: https://handle.me, which will detect the $acme Handle and allow them to mint NFT-based subHandles, issue and revoke Virtual subHandles. The project will also deliver a decentralized API endpoint that will allow projects to perform API queries for Handles and subHandles, delivering all data associated with them.
ms.criteria: The acceptance criteria for MainNet launch of subHandles is a working product, integrated to our handle.me portal, that the community can connect their wallets to, in order to mint subHandles. The feature will identify Handles owned by users, by verifying their ownership twice, once upon connecting the wallet and a second time prior to minting subHandles.
